title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.
intro: This training programme equips investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud and cyber-enabled financial crime, from push payment and investment scams to money mule networks and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to support victims and recover funds.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give investigators and analysts a practical understanding of how modern fraud and cyber-enabled crime generate and move proceeds at speed and scale. Participants leave able to recognise the main typologies, act quickly with banks and payment firms to freeze and trace funds, dismantle money mule networks, support victims and pursue recovery.
sections.What It Covers: The fraud and cyber-enabled crime landscape, authorised push payment and impersonation fraud, investment and online scam platforms, money mule networks, ransomware and its proceeds, rapid response with banks and payment firms, victim support and prevention, and recovery and disruption.
Intended Audience: Fraud, economic crime and cybercrime investigators
FIU analysts handling fraud-related reports and urgent requests
Victim liaison, prevention and disruption officers working with the financial sector
Learning Objectives: Explain the main fraud and cyber-enabled crime typologies and how proceeds move
Identify money mule activity and the networks that recruit and control mules
Trace scam and ransomware proceeds across payment and crypto-asset channels
Work with banks and payment firms to freeze, repatriate and recover funds quickly
Support victims effectively and reduce repeat victimisation
Design disruption and prevention responses alongside prosecution
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies and response exercises, ending in an investigation workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the participants' caseload and partners.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, cybercrime or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in cyber security or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2023), Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-Enabled Fraud
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers

modules.title: The Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Crime Landscape
modules.summary: The scale and nature of fraud and cyber-enabled financial crime, the organised groups behind it, and why speed, volume and cross-border reach challenge traditional investigation.
objectives: Describe the main categories of fraud and cyber-enabled financial crime
Explain the organisation and business models of fraud networks
Identify the challenges these crimes pose for investigation and prosecution
syllabus: Fraud as a high-volume, organised and transnational crime
Social engineering and the industrialisation of scams
Victim and loss data: reporting, under-reporting and triage
International assessments of cyber-enabled fraud

modules.title: Authorised Push Payment and Impersonation Fraud
modules.summary: How victims are manipulated into authorising payments to criminals, the main scam types, and the evidence available from victims, banks and communications providers.
objectives: Explain how authorised push payment fraud differs from unauthorised fraud
Recognise impersonation, invoice redirection and purchase scams
Gather evidence from victims, banks and communications providers
syllabus: Authorised versus unauthorised payment fraud
Impersonation, business email compromise and invoice redirection
Purchase, advance fee and romance scams
Evidence sources: victim accounts, payment records and communications data

modules.title: Investment Fraud and Online Scam Platforms
modules.summary: How fake investment platforms, crypto-asset scams and boiler rooms operate, how they move victim funds, and how investigators identify the people and infrastructure behind them.
objectives: Recognise the features of investment fraud and fake trading platforms
Trace victim funds through payment and crypto-asset channels
Identify the infrastructure and actors behind scam operations
syllabus: Boiler rooms, clone firms and fake trading platforms
Crypto-asset and relationship investment scams
Payment routes, intermediary accounts and off-ramps
Websites, domains, advertising and scam infrastructure

modules.title: Money Mule Networks
modules.summary: How mule accounts are recruited, controlled and used to layer fraud proceeds, how to distinguish witting from unwitting mules, and how to dismantle the networks behind them.
objectives: Explain how mule networks are recruited and controlled
Identify indicators of mule accounts in financial data
Choose proportionate responses for different types of mule
syllabus: Mule recruitment, herders and controllers
Indicators of mule activity in account and payment data
Witting, unwitting and complicit mules
Network analysis and targeting controllers

modules.title: Ransomware and Cyber-Enabled Proceeds
modules.summary: How ransomware and other cyber-enabled crimes generate proceeds, how payments are made and laundered, and how investigators trace and seek to recover them.
objectives: Explain the ransomware business model and payment process
Trace ransom payments and their laundering through crypto-asset channels
Coordinate with victims, incident responders and service providers
syllabus: Ransomware-as-a-service and affiliate models
Ransom payments, reporting and engagement with victims
Laundering and cash-out of crypto-asset proceeds
Seizure and recovery opportunities

modules.title: Working with Banks and Payment Firms: Rapid Response
modules.summary: How law enforcement and FIUs work with banks, payment and e-money firms and crypto-asset service providers to freeze, trace and repatriate fraud proceeds within hours rather than weeks.
objectives: Use rapid-response and freezing mechanisms with financial institutions
Request and interpret payment, account and device data
Build effective working relationships and escalation routes with the private sector
syllabus: Rapid freezing, recall and repatriation of funds
Payment, account, device and login data from institutions
Single points of contact and escalation routes
Data-sharing gateways and public-private fraud partnerships

modules.title: Victim Support and Prevention
modules.summary: How investigators support victims through reporting, investigation and recovery, reduce repeat victimisation, and contribute to prevention and public awareness.
objectives: Apply a victim-centred approach throughout the investigation
Identify vulnerable and repeat victims and refer them for support
Contribute to prevention, warnings and disruption campaigns
syllabus: Victim needs, vulnerability and trauma-informed engagement
Repeat victimisation and recovery scams
Reimbursement, compensation and restitution routes
Prevention: alerts, warnings and takedowns

modules.title: Recovery, Disruption and Investigation Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams respond to a cross-border scam, freeze and trace funds, support victims and agree prosecution, recovery and disruption actions.
objectives: Apply typologies, tracing and rapid response to a realistic case
Balance prosecution, recovery and disruption objectives
Agree a coordinated response across agencies and the private sector
syllabus: Case briefing: a cross-border investment scam and mule network
Freezing, tracing and evidence-gathering exercise
Recovery, compensation and disruption options
Workshop: the coordinated response plan

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
